title: Board Game Cafés: A Rainy Day Out for Families and Teens
description: Board game cafés for families and teens: how cover charges work, staff who teach the rules, games for all ages, and why they suit rainy days.
h1: Board game cafés: a rainy day out for families and teens
intro: Hundreds of games, someone to teach you the rules, and snacks on tap. Board game cafés are a brilliant rainy-day out that gets teens off their phones.

image.alt: A neon sign for escape rooms

cardText: How cover charges work, games for all ages and why teens love them.

blocks.title: Scout’s game-night tip
blocks.text: Ask the staff for a recommendation. Tell them your ages and how long you’ve got, and they’ll pick a winner.
points: Check the age policy (some are 18+ in the evening)
Quick party games suit mixed ages

sections.html: Most board game cafés charge a per-person table or cover fee for a set time, with food and drinks on top. You can play anything from the library, and staff often teach the rules.

• Little ones: simple co-operative games and matching games.
  • Ages 8+: quick card games and family strategy games.
  • Teens: party and bluffing games, plus bigger strategy games.
Pair it with a museum or the cinema. See indoor fun, rainy day ideas and escape rooms for more puzzle fun.

faqs.q: Are board game cafés good for kids?
faqs.a: Many welcome families during the day and have games for young children. Some are adults-only in the evenings, so check the age policy.
